standard: GDD rework v2 · 80+ researched scenarios · scorecard-passed
note: Choosing a partner & what makes a healthy long-term partnership/marriage, love & arranged; commitment & communication (UNESCO 1.2, 1.4, 5.3, 2.1). New v2 build, opening Chapter 7 (Building a Life), where the story turns from 'me' to 'us'. A wedding is a day; a partnership is the work. Five modes: choosing well (values & compatibility over sparks and timeline), what it takes (communication, trust, repair, interdependence, build us without erasing me), commitment clearly (thoughtful, eyes-open; bust 'marriage will fix/complete me'; UN&RE), love & arranged (both paths, the same skills; consent essential in any path; family involvement respected but the couple's judgement leads; forced marriage routed to help), starting strong (expectations, communication, equality from day one), tools/help. Every path respected, including not marrying (the counterpoint g54); no pressure toward or against marriage. Consent and respect carried from g31/g44. Builds on g46 (Real Relationships) and g31 (Mutual); sets up Equal Partners (g55) and The Family Map (g57). India: marriage is the central life event, both arranged and love, with relational pressures (timeline, in-laws, 'log kya kahenge'); coercion or forced marriage routed to help (181, 1091, 112, Childline 1098).

evidenceBase: Choosing a partner well means weighing values, respect, shared goals and compatibility, not just chemistry: research consistently finds that value alignment and practical compatibility predict relationship satisfaction far better than initial spark, and as the saying goes, chemistry draws you together while compatibility keeps you together. The deep green flags are respect, kindness, how someone treats others and handles conflict and shared core values; the red flags are control, contempt, dishonesty and incompatible values, and how a person behaves under stress and disagreement reveals them (compatibility-vs-chemistry research; Gottman shared-values agreement)

A lasting partnership is built, not just felt: communication, trust, repair after conflict and interdependence (a team of two whole people, building 'us' without erasing 'me') are the daily work, and Gottman finds couples who agree on important values and how to resolve conflict stay happy long-term. Commitment is best approached with eyes open and thoughtfully, from genuine choice rather than pressure, timeline or drift, and the myth that 'marriage will fix our problems or complete me' is false, a partnership is built by two whole people, not a cure for problems or loneliness (Gottman; long-term-relationship research)

Every path is respected and consent is central: love marriage, an arranged match and long-term partnership are all valid and need the same foundations of values, compatibility and communication, the arranged process can carry the same values-and-compatibility lens with real questions and time, and consent is essential in any path, with the right to say yes or no and to take time. Family involvement can be respected while the couple's own judgement and consent lead, and coercion or forced marriage is never acceptable and is routed to help; not marrying is an equally valid path. Equality is built in from day one through honest early conversations about money, work, roles and expectations (UNESCO ITGSE KC1; consent and forced-marriage safeguarding)

scenarios.hook: "Choose a partner on chemistry and sparks alone."

myth.un: Choose a partner on chemistry and sparks alone.
myth.re: Compatibility and shared values are what keep love going; chemistry draws you together, compatibility keeps you together.
myth.why: Spark fades; shared values and respect last.

scenarios.relearn: Compatibility and shared values keep love going; chemistry alone doesn't.

scenarios.hook: Sort: a deep green flag for a long-term partner, or just surface appeal?

items.text: Treats waiters and elders with respect

scenarios.relearn: How they treat others and handle conflict is a deep green flag; looks and status are surface.

scenarios.hook: You're drawn to someone exciting, but your core values clearly clash.

options.text: Weigh the values mismatch seriously, not just the spark
options.consequence: You choose with your eyes open.

options.text: Ignore it; the chemistry is amazing
options.consequence: Spark fades and value clashes grow; weighing compatibility seriously is how lasting choices are made.

scenarios.debrief: Exciting chemistry can't carry a partnership through clashing core values; weigh both.
scenarios.relearn: Take a values mismatch seriously, even when the chemistry is strong.

scenarios.hook: "How someone treats you when calm is the real them."

myth.un: How someone treats you when calm is the real them.
myth.re: How a person behaves under stress, disagreement and when they don't get their way reveals them most.
myth.why: Anyone is pleasant when things are easy.

scenarios.relearn: How someone behaves under stress and disagreement reveals them most.

scenarios.hook: Match what to weigh in a long-term partner to why.
scenarios.relearn: Shared values, conflict-handling and respect are what to weigh in a long-term partner.

scenarios.hook: Family is pushing a match mainly on caste, status and looks.

options.text: Apply your own values-and-compatibility lens too
options.consequence: You bring real judgement to the choice.

options.text: Decide on status and looks alone
options.consequence: A values-and-compatibility lens, alongside any family input, leads to better long-term choices than status alone.

scenarios.debrief: Whatever the route, weighing values and compatibility yourself leads to a sounder choice.
scenarios.relearn: Apply your own values-and-compatibility lens, not just status and looks.

scenarios.hook: Spot the long-term green flag.

scene.text: They listen and own their mistakes

scenarios.why: Listening, owning mistakes and respecting boundaries are green flags; love-bombing then cold isn't.
scenarios.relearn: Listening, owning mistakes and respecting boundaries are long-term green flags.

scenarios.hook: "Red flags will sort themselves out once you're committed."

myth.un: Red flags will sort themselves out once you're committed.
myth.re: Commitment rarely fixes red flags like control or contempt; they tend to grow.

scenarios.relearn: Commitment rarely fixes red flags; control and contempt tend to grow, not vanish.

scenarios.hook: Spot the shift away from a costly partner-choosing pattern.
scenarios.relearn: Shift from choosing on thrill to valuing steadiness, respect and fit.
scenarios.why: Valuing steadiness, respect and compatibility is the healthy shift; chasing only thrill repeats the pattern.

scenarios.hook: Sam: the question isn't just 'do I like them?' but 'can we build a good life together?'. Useful shift?
scenarios.affirm: 'Can we build a life together?' is the question that finds a real partner, not just a spark.
scenarios.relearn: Ask not just 'do I like them?' but 'can we build a good life together?'.

scenarios.hook: Sort: a sign of real compatibility, or just infatuation?

items.text: You want similar things from life
You can't stop thinking about them

scenarios.relearn: Wanting similar things and resolving conflict well is compatibility; intensity alone is infatuation.

scenarios.hook: Sam: take your time choosing; this is one of the biggest decisions you'll make. Permission to go slow?
scenarios.affirm: Taking real time to choose a life partner is wisdom, not indecision; there's no prize for rushing.
scenarios.relearn: Take your time choosing a partner; it's one of life's biggest decisions.

scenarios.hook: "If you really love each other, you won't need to work at it."

myth.un: If you really love each other, you won't need to work at it.
myth.re: Every lasting partnership takes communication, trust and repair; love is built, not just felt.
myth.why: Even great couples do the daily work.

scenarios.relearn: Every lasting partnership takes work; love is built, not just felt.

scenarios.hook: Sort: builds a lasting partnership, or erodes it?
scenarios.relearn: Repair and appreciation build a partnership; piled-up resentment and scorekeeping erode it.

scenarios.hook: You want to raise something that's been bothering you, kindly.
scenarios.setup: Lead with how you feel. Say:

yourLine.text: "I've felt a bit unheard lately, can we talk about it?"
"You never listen to me."

scenarios.relearn: Raise an issue with an 'I felt...' opener, not a 'you never' attack.

scenarios.hook: "A good partnership means becoming one person and losing yourself."

myth.un: A partnership means losing yourself in the other.
myth.re: Healthy partnership is interdependence, a team of two whole people; build 'us' without erasing 'me'.
myth.why: Two whole people make the strongest team.

scenarios.relearn: Healthy partnership is two whole people as a team; build 'us' without erasing 'me'.

scenarios.hook: You and your partner keep having the same argument unresolved.

options.text: Get underneath it: what each of you really needs
options.consequence: You move from fighting to understanding.

options.text: Keep rehashing the surface fight
options.consequence: Getting underneath to each person's real need resolves a recurring fight better than rehashing the surface.

scenarios.debrief: Recurring fights usually hide unmet needs; addressing those, not the surface, is the work.
scenarios.relearn: For a recurring argument, get underneath to what each of you really needs.

scenarios.hook: Sort: builds trust in a partnership, or breaks it?
scenarios.relearn: Promises kept and reliability build trust; hiding things and breaking confidences break it.

scenarios.hook: Your partner did something kind and you want to nurture the bond.

yourLine.text: "I really appreciated that, thank you, it meant a lot."
Assume they know without saying it

scenarios.relearn: Express appreciation out loud; it's small to do and big for the bond.

scenarios.hook: Sam: a strong partnership is two people turning toward each other, again and again. Recognise that?
scenarios.affirm: Turning toward each other in the small moments is what quietly builds a lasting bond.
scenarios.relearn: A strong partnership is two people turning toward each other, again and again.

scenarios.hook: Life gets busy and you've stopped really talking with your partner.

options.text: Protect regular time to connect and check in
options.consequence: You keep the partnership alive under pressure.

options.text: Let the connection drift indefinitely
options.consequence: Protecting regular time to connect keeps a partnership alive; drift quietly erodes it.

scenarios.debrief: Partnerships need protected time to connect; busyness is when it matters most.
scenarios.relearn: Protect regular time to connect; don't let busyness erode the bond.

scenarios.hook: Sort: interdependence, or losing yourself?

items.text: Keeping your own friends and interests

scenarios.relearn: Keeping your own life and supporting each other's growth is interdependence; giving up everything is losing yourself.

scenarios.hook: "Marriage will fix our problems and complete me."

myth.un: Marriage will fix our problems and complete me.
myth.re: A partnership is built by two whole people; it isn't a cure for problems or loneliness.
myth.why: Commitment amplifies what's already there, good and bad.

scenarios.relearn: Marriage isn't a cure for problems or loneliness; a partnership is built by two whole people.

scenarios.hook: "A wedding is the goal; after that it's all sorted."

myth.un: A wedding is the goal; after that it's sorted.
myth.re: A wedding is a day; the partnership is the ongoing work that follows.
myth.why: The real life begins after the celebration.

scenarios.relearn: A wedding is a day; the partnership is the ongoing work.

scenarios.hook: You feel pressured to commit because of your age and what people will say.

options.text: Commit only when you genuinely choose it, not from pressure
options.consequence: You make a sounder, freer choice.

options.text: Marry to silence the questions
options.consequence: Committing from genuine choice, not age-and-pressure, makes for a far sounder marriage.

scenarios.debrief: Marrying to escape pressure or timelines rarely ends well; commitment should be a real choice.
scenarios.relearn: Commit when you genuinely choose it, not from pressure or timeline.

scenarios.hook: "You should commit because everyone your age is settling down."

myth.un: You should commit because everyone your age is settling down.
myth.re: Your timeline is your own; drifting into commitment to match others rarely lasts.

scenarios.relearn: Your timeline is your own; don't drift into commitment to match others.

scenarios.hook: Sort: a sound reason to commit, or a shaky one?

items.text: You choose this person and the work
You've talked through the real stuff

scenarios.relearn: Choosing the person and having talked things through is sound; social pressure and fear of being alone are shaky.

scenarios.hook: Before committing, there are big topics you've both avoided.

options.text: Talk them through honestly before you commit
options.consequence: You commit with eyes open.

options.text: Assume it'll work itself out after
options.consequence: Talking through the big topics before committing beats hoping they sort themselves out after.

scenarios.debrief: Eyes-open commitment means discussing the big things, money, children, roles, before, not after.
scenarios.relearn: Talk through the big topics honestly before you commit.

scenarios.hook: Sam: commitment works best as a clear, free choice, not pressure or drift. Sit right with you?
scenarios.affirm: A clear, freely-chosen commitment is the strongest foundation; pressure and drift are weak ones.
scenarios.relearn: Commitment works best as a clear, free choice, not pressure or drift.

scenarios.hook: Sam: choosing not to commit, or to wait, is an equally valid, respectable path. Agree?
scenarios.affirm: Not committing, or waiting, is a wholly valid path; this is your life to shape.
scenarios.relearn: Choosing not to commit, or to wait, is an equally valid path.

scenarios.hook: "An arranged match means you have no choice or consent."

myth.un: An arranged match means no choice or consent.
myth.re: Consent is essential in any path; you have the right to say yes or no and to take your time.
myth.why: A match is a proposal, not a command.

scenarios.relearn: Consent is essential in any path; you have the right to say yes or no and to take time.

scenarios.hook: "Love marriages and arranged marriages need completely different things."

myth.un: Love and arranged marriages need completely different things.
myth.re: Both need the same foundations: values, compatibility, communication and consent.
myth.why: The path differs; the skills don't.

scenarios.relearn: Love and arranged marriages need the same foundations: values, compatibility, communication, consent.

scenarios.hook: In an arranged-match process, you're rushed to decide quickly.

options.text: Ask for time and real conversations first
options.consequence: You bring judgement and consent to it.

options.text: Just say yes to avoid making waves
options.consequence: Asking for time and real conversations brings your judgement and consent in, rather than being rushed.

scenarios.debrief: You can apply a values-and-compatibility lens, ask real questions, and take time in any process.
scenarios.relearn: In an arranged process, ask for time and real conversations before deciding.

scenarios.hook: Match the question to what it reveals about a match.
scenarios.relearn: Asking about goals, conflict style and values reveals real fit.

pairs.left: "What do you want from a partnership?"

scenarios.hook: "Family knows best; the couple's own judgement doesn't really matter."

myth.un: Family knows best; the couple's judgement doesn't matter.
myth.re: Family involvement can be respected, but the couple's own judgement and consent should lead.
myth.why: They're the ones who'll live the marriage.

scenarios.relearn: Family involvement can be respected, but the couple's own judgement and consent should lead.

scenarios.hook: You're being pressured into a marriage you don't consent to.

options.text: Hold your no; forced marriage is never okay, and there's help
options.consequence: You protect your right to choose.

options.text: Give in because the family insists

scenarios.debrief: A marriage without your consent is forced marriage, which is never acceptable; help exists.
scenarios.relearn: Forced marriage is never okay; your consent is required, and help exists (181, 1098, 112).

yourLine.text: "I value your input, and I need a little more time and a few real conversations first."
Cave to the timeline to keep the peace

scenarios.relearn: You can respectfully ask family for more time and real conversations before deciding.

scenarios.hook: Sam: love marriage, arranged, or partnership, every path is valid, and consent makes it yours. Agree?
scenarios.affirm: Whatever the path, your consent and judgement are what make the choice truly yours.
scenarios.relearn: Every path is valid; your consent and judgement make the choice yours.

scenarios.hook: Sort: respects the couple, or overrides them?

items.text: Forcing a match against a no
Giving the couple time to know each other

scenarios.relearn: Suggesting-but-couple-deciding and giving time respects them; forcing against a no overrides them.

scenarios.hook: Your relationship doesn't fit the traditional married-man-and-woman mould.

options.text: Build the partnership that's right for you two
options.consequence: You honour your own path.

options.text: Force it into a mould that doesn't fit
options.consequence: Building the partnership that's right for you two beats forcing it into a mould that doesn't fit.

scenarios.debrief: Partnerships come in many valid forms; the skills of values, communication and respect apply to all.
scenarios.relearn: Build the partnership that's right for you two; many forms are valid.

scenarios.hook: "Talking about money, roles and expectations before marriage is unromantic."

myth.un: Talking about money, roles and expectations is unromantic.
myth.re: Those early conversations are how you start strong and avoid painful surprises later.

scenarios.relearn: Early talks about money, roles and expectations start a partnership strong, not unromantic.

scenarios.hook: You're about to start a life together and haven't discussed how you'll share the load.

options.text: Agree on a fair share of work and money from the start
options.consequence: You build equality in from day one.

options.text: Let traditional roles just happen by default
options.consequence: Agreeing a fair share from the start builds equality in; default roles quietly create imbalance.

scenarios.debrief: Building equality in from day one is far easier than renegotiating an unfair default later.
scenarios.relearn: Agree a fair share of work and money from the start; don't default to roles.

scenarios.hook: You want to set a tone of equal partnership early with your partner.

yourLine.text: "Let's build this as equals, sharing the load and the decisions, from the start."
Assume the roles will just sort themselves out

scenarios.relearn: Name the intention to build as equals early; don't leave roles to default.

scenarios.hook: Spot the strong start to a partnership.
scenarios.relearn: Honest talks and agreeing how to handle conflict start a partnership strong.
scenarios.why: Honest talks and agreeing how to handle conflict start strong; avoiding topics doesn't.

scenarios.hook: Your families have very different expectations of your new marriage.

options.text: Decide together as a couple-unit how to navigate it
options.consequence: You set healthy boundaries early.

options.text: Let each family pull you separately
options.consequence: Deciding together as a couple-unit, and setting boundaries, navigates family expectations better than being pulled apart.

scenarios.debrief: Facing family expectations as a united couple-unit, with kind boundaries, sets up the years ahead.
scenarios.relearn: Navigate family expectations together as a couple-unit, with kind boundaries.

scenarios.hook: Spot the early habit that sets a partnership up well.
scenarios.relearn: The habits you build early set the pattern; start with communication and repair.
scenarios.why: Open communication and early repair set a partnership up well; avoiding hard topics doesn't.

scenarios.hook: Sort: a conversation worth having early, or one to skip?

items.text: Whether and when to have children
How money will work between you

scenarios.hook: Match the partnership tool to what it's for.

scenarios.hook: Match the sign to what it tells you about a partnership.

scenarios.hook: Match the partnership step to what it does.

scenarios.hook: A friend is choosing a partner mostly to satisfy family and timeline.

options.text: Tell them to just get it over with
options.consequence: Encouraging a friend to weigh values and their own choice helps more than 'just get it done'.

scenarios.hook: Sort: a reliable basis for a partnership, or a fragile one?
scenarios.relearn: Shared values, respect and communication are reliable; chemistry-only and hoping-they'll-change are fragile.

scenarios.hook: Spot the wise response to a persistent 'something's off' feeling.

scenarios.hook: You love each other but want very different things from life.

options.text: Assume love will paper over it

scenarios.hook: Sam: meeting a few times in an arranged process is choosing, too, you're allowed to weigh it. Reassuring?

scenarios.hook: Spot the foundation of a lasting partnership.

myth.un: Any doubts before commitment mean it's definitely wrong.
myth.re: Some nerves are normal; persistent doubts about core respect or values, though, are worth heeding.
myth.why: Distinguish ordinary nerves from real red flags.

scenarios.relearn: Some nerves are normal; but persistent doubts about core respect or values are worth heeding.

scenarios.hook: Sam: whatever path you choose, the goal is a partnership of equals built on consent and respect. Carry that?
scenarios.affirm: A partnership of equals, built on consent and respect, is the goal on every path.
scenarios.relearn: On any path, the goal is a partnership of equals built on consent and respect.

scenarios.hook: You and your partner come from families with different traditions and expectations.

options.text: Talk through which traditions you'll keep, blend or set aside, together
options.consequence: You build your own shared culture.

options.text: Let one family's way simply win
options.consequence: Deciding together which traditions to keep, blend or set aside builds a shared culture better than one side winning.

scenarios.debrief: Building a partnership often means consciously creating your own shared culture from two backgrounds.
scenarios.relearn: Decide together which traditions to keep, blend or set aside; build your own shared culture.

scenarios.hook: Sam: a couples counsellor isn't only for crises, plenty of strong couples use one to build better. Reframe?
scenarios.affirm: Counselling is a tool for building a stronger partnership, not only for fixing a broken one.
scenarios.relearn: A couples counsellor is for building better, not only for crises.

scenarios.hook: Sort: something this game stands for, or against?

items.text: Respecting every path, including not marrying
Treating a wedding as the whole goal

scenarios.relearn: Choosing on values and respecting every path is the stance; pressuring to marry or wedding-as-goal isn't.

scenarios.hook: Sam: choose well, build with care, commit freely, which will you carry into your own partnership?
scenarios.affirm: Carry that one, and you're set to build a partnership that genuinely lasts, on your own terms.
scenarios.relearn: Values over sparks, partnership is built, commit with eyes open, every path with consent.
